title: Prove exact rounding radii for signed-permutation frame groups (no κ)
body:
## Summary

Prove the exact least uniform rounding radius for every integer change of basis of the full signed-permutation group. Claim type: scoped written mathematical proof with exact finite corroboration, produced by Nick Petalas.

```text
P in GL_d(Z), G=P B_d P^-1, L=max absolute row sum of P
complete (1/m)Z^d -> Z^d:  R_m=floor(m/2)*L/m
all R^d -> Z^d:             R=L/2
attaining rule:             q(x)=P nearest_odd(P^-1 x)
```

The lower bound applies to every equivariant function, including arbitrary coupled nonlinear rounders: an explicit point stabilizer forces its output onto a primitive integer line. One half-tie-away rule attains the bound for the whole group and fixes integer inputs. Scaling the output grid scales the radius.

This answers the signed-permutation conjugacy class of Krzysztof Wojt's released larger-finite-group question in [PR5122](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/5122), head `dab8cc5917fbc76564367a973bd6cd1ed5a22ee3`. Nick Petalas's [PR5079](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/5079), head `43f558c1b8fc14fb0ed33a4512fbc976beea6b0f`, supplies the existence context and sheared-dihedral example. The reflection subgroup's numerical lower value is already PR5122's result; the new result supplies simultaneous attainment for all frames and the general P,d formula. Neither predecessor executable is replayed or audited.

Start with [PROOF.md](https://github.com/petalas/integer-mult-bounds/blob/e8a55a6edf91c5067b26cdfefbcc76517f86ab02/research/signed-permutation-frame-radius/PROOF.md) and [README.md](https://github.com/petalas/integer-mult-bounds/blob/e8a55a6edf91c5067b26cdfefbcc76517f86ab02/research/signed-permutation-frame-radius/README.md). [Advance CLAIM](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-19370162).

## Evidence

- Before: PR5122 settles order-two reflections and explicitly leaves simultaneous larger finite groups open. After: the written proof gives matching upper/lower bounds for every conjugated full signed-permutation group in every dimension.
- All 104 unimodular two-by-two frames with entries in [-2,2], denominators 2 through 9 and their complete transformed residue sets: 29,536 points and 236,288 literal equivariance comparisons.
- An independent integer-only physical-orbit oracle tests every stabilizer and every integer candidate in a complete incumbent-derived box. Across that domain and 832 explicit attaining orbits it enumerates 99,264 output candidates. It imports no radius formula, rounder, inverse routine or predecessor code.
- Eight further frames through dimension eight: 680 rational points, 5,440 generator comparisons and 140 fixed-point checks. Five semantic controls, an actual nonodd-tie mutation, fifteen invalid-input rejections and a 257-bit integer-fixing case pass.
- Warning-strict CPython 3.12.15 normal and optimized registered checks pass locally, about 3.5 seconds each, under their separate 180-second limits. Generated receipts agree byte for byte. Metadata/source pins, eight-file committed bytes/modes and declared source history pass at `e8a55a6edf91c5067b26cdfefbcc76517f86ab02`.
- Official export integrity/input coverage and both direct read-only, Git-free, empty-PATH replays pass; all nine export files retain their hashes and modes. Both exported commands take about 3.46 seconds. These are replay-deadline measurements, not a performance-improvement claim.

From the repository root, using the exact local interpreter path:

```sh
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -I -W error -B research/signed-permutation-frame-radius/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -I -O -W error -B research/signed-permutation-frame-radius/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/signed-permutation-frame-radius
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/check_research_commit.py --package research/signed-permutation-frame-radius --check-source-history --check-modes
```

Another CPython 3.12 executable may replace that path. Expected markers are `PASS_SIGNED_PERMUTATION_FRAME_RADIUS`, `PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE` and `PASS_RESEARCH_COMMIT_BYTES`. The direct verifier writes no files by default; its optional receipt is generated and bound to source hashes. There are no external runtime inputs.

## Limitations

The `uniform-transfer-audit` card changes explicitly to this precision side theorem. The complete refined grid or all-real domain is essential; no current reader is shown to reach its maximizing point. Other integral representations, changing grids, frame-dependent rules and restricted reachable domains require separate analysis. The universal conclusion rests on the written proof rather than finite extrapolation.

No physical rounding circuit, dirty restoration, native supplier, movement/stock/precision/tape invoice, compiler or outer admission is supplied. There is no new kappa or selected-frontier change. All five selected framework assumptions remain. Selected cold replay, Lean, Docker, independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed. No required package check is left solely to CI.

## Open next questions

- Pin one actual carried reader, its frame P and complete dirty-input image, then decide whether it reaches the explicit maximizing orbit. Reachability and a complete paid rounding/restoration bill remain missing.
- Determine an exact stabilizer-compatible radius for one finite integral representation outside the signed-permutation conjugacy class. Start with its fixed sublattices; this proof supplies no general finite-group radius algorithm.

## Related open work

No open PR was identified studying this same equivariant integer-frame-group radius. The merged PR5122 and PR5079 are the direct context.

- [PR6492](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/6492) accelerates a characteristic-two D8 group-ring word replay. Its common abstract group name does not give it this integer-frame rounding contract; no shared numerical optimum is compared.
- [PR6536](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/6536) concerns a three-axis Gaussian coset rounding problem, with different matrices and admissibility conditions. No radius for that contract is computed here.
- [PR6540](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/6540) concerns unbiased native coarsening and a retained residue codec. Its mean-squared-error and state-capacity quantities differ from this exact equivariance/minimax problem.

- [PR6564](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/6564) proves a rounded dyadic connector carry formula under a specified scalar query and root-restoration contract. This contribution instead optimizes exact equivariance for a whole integer frame group on the complete grid; no competing value for either contract is computed.

Before DONE, the completion refresh inspected all fifteen other account open PRs created since the advance CLAIM at 2026-11-03T09:05:08Z. They study replay implementations, connector capacity or pruning, norm-six denominators, rank-two headers, rounded connector carry, polynomial target costs, G20 state, a nilpotent chain, R439 taps, JP8 continuation and reserve ratios. None studies this same integer-frame-group/grid contract or reports a competing value for its radius. No additional scientific computations checked another contribution.

Live open PRs, handoff claims and local reservations were refreshed before committing. Canonical main remained `7c49fe32c55de02c2c873655c804b16e4c3fef0a`, priority revision 8, selected PR6030. The overlap snapshot covered 505 open PRs and 6,496 Discussion records; main README and merged/all-state object/formula searches were also checked. Unpublished work and arbitrary historical diffs remain outside coverage.
